exam.title: Professional Cloud Security Engineer
exam.study_prerequisites: No formal prerequisite; Google recommends three or more years of industry experience including at least one year on Google Cloud. Practice workforce/workload identity and privilege, NGFW/private/perimeter controls, sensitive-data/key/secret/AI protection, secure supply chain/posture, centralized logging/detection/response, and compliance scope/control/evidence using authorized disposable environments.

objective_coverage.objective_group: Securing communications and establishing boundary protection (~22%)

review.notes: All five current defensive domains are mapped through threat/obligation, preventive control, negative/positive validation, telemetry, response/recovery and evidence. Three scenarios, eight authorized labs and 36 checks cover identity, boundaries, data/AI protection, supply chain/posture/SecOps and compliance. All seven URLs are cataloged: six reachable and O'Reilly automation-blocked; none missing or broken. No exploit target, proprietary bank, recalled item or copied course content is used.

findings.title: Missing lifecycle field does not imply absent validity terms
A conditional allow cannot narrow an unconditional grant
Deny evaluation has separate condition and inheritance semantics
Key deletion does not revoke previously issued credentials
Shared issuers and reusable names need scoped immutable trust
PAM entitlement does not universally require approval or offer every approval feature
Rotation schedule delivers a notification instead of completing credential rollout
Wrapped-key changes and payload encryption have different guarantees
Preview and body inspection have distinct enforcement boundaries
Data Access evidence needs explicit source and reader coverage
A retained breakglass annotation can affect later deployments
Provider access approval has enrollment and documented exceptions
